title: 2025 Statistical Summary of Commercial Jet Airplane Accidents

verified_observations.publication: The inspected edition is dated April 2026 and describes worldwide operations through 2025.
verified_observations.annual_accident_rates: Report contains accident rates and onboard fatalities by year, 1959-2025, per one million departures.
verified_observations.aggregate_exposure: Report contains worldwide departures and flight-hours over time for 2006-2025 and reports cumulative Boeing-vs-total shares.
verified_observations.aggregate_2025: The report states 33.1 million departures and 78.3 million flight-hours for the worldwide commercial jet fleet in 2025, plus 30,660 airplanes in service, of which 14,031 are Boeing airplanes.
verified_observations.cumulative_boeing_share: The report states 998 million departures since 1959, 62% on Boeing airplanes (622 million), and 1,969 million flight-hours since 1959, 63% on Boeing airplanes (1,249 million).
verified_observations.airplane_type_rates: Report contains cumulative hull-loss accident rates by airplane type; types with fewer than one million departures are explicitly marked.
verified_observations.current_year_event_table: Report contains event-level 2025 airplane accident summaries.
verified_observations.rate_denominator_method: Boeing states that departures/flight cycles are the basis for accident rates and that departure data are continually updated and revised.

limitations: The verified 2025 report does not by itself provide a machine-readable event-level 2010-2025 Boeing-only census matching BSFM target semantics.
The annual worldwide departures/flight-hours chart is fleet aggregate, not a demonstrated Boeing-family-by-year denominator table.
The Boeing-vs-total departure and flight-hour shares are cumulative since 1959, not annual family-level exposure.
Cumulative airplane-type accident rates or cumulative Boeing shares must not be inverted, interpolated or disaggregated to manufacture annual family exposure.
Boeing report inclusion/exclusion definitions must be reconciled with the BSFM target before G1 attestation.
